subject: Re: Follow-up: LegacyBank on-prem / air-gapped deployment questions
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: on-prem / air-gapped deployment questions

Tom — great to meet earlier. Quick recap + a few follow-ups from today's discovery so we can size the on-prem/air-gapped POC: 

Summary of what I heard:
- Goal: private, air-gapped deployment for customer-facing LLM features (PII-sensitive workflows).
- Preferred deployment: Private/on-prem (no outbound internet from inference cluster).
- Ideal POC: 4–8 GPU nodes with ability to scale to ~16 nodes in production.

Questions for sizing and architecture (can you confirm?):
1) Hardware baseline: do you expect to use existing fleet (can you share GPU make/model + memory per GPU) or will LegacyBank procure new nodes?
2) Upgrade policy: are maintenance windows restricted to monthly/quarterly windows? Any blackout dates?
3) Network constraints: will the cluster be fully air-gapped (no egress) or allowed controlled egress to a jump host for signed update bundles?
4) KMS/HSM: do you have a preferred HSM vendor (AWS CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault HSM, Thales) or will Redwood need to provide an integrated approach?

Next steps I propose:
- You share a brief infra snapshot (GPU model, node count, OS image).
- We run a 2-week POC plan (we'll provide an offline install bundle + signed artifacts).
- Tech deep-dive call with our engineers (Dev + Vivek) to confirm upgrade/backup flow and support SLAs.

Attaching a short deployment requirements doc (stub) to help collect the infra details.

Thanks — if any of the summary points above are off, flag and I’ll correct.

Best,

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@legacybank.com>

Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 09:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Follow-up: on-prem / air-gapped deployment questions

Thanks Marissa — good summary. Answers inline below.

Hardware: We're looking at using our new procurement but can run a POC on the test cluster. Current test cluster spec: 8x NVIDIA A100 40GB (2U nodes, 4 GPUs per node) running RHEL 8.6. Production target: 16x A100 80GB across 4 nodes (planned purchase Q3).

Upgrade policy: Maintenance windows are monthly (first Sunday 00:00–06:00 local). We have strict blackout windows around quarter ends.

Network: For the POC we can enable a jump-host with tightly controlled egress to fetch signed update bundles (IP allowlist + mutual TLS). Production will be fully air-gapped but we can do signed bundles via removable media or customer-managed jump host.

KMS/HSM: We use an on-prem Thales HSM for key material. We can provide an integration point (PKCS#11).

Other asks from my side:
- Can you confirm offline upgrade packaging (how do you verify signatures) and rollback story?
- What level of on-prem support/responsiveness do you offer for air-gapped deployments? SLA windows?

Attaching a simple infra diagram for context.

–Tom
Tom Reynolds
Director, Emerging Tech — LegacyBank
tom.reynolds@legacybank.com

Attachment: legacybank_infra_diagram.pdf (1 page)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: on-prem / air-gapped deployment questions

Perfect — thanks for the details, Tom. Short answers and what we’ll provide for the POC: 

1) Offline upgrade packaging: we produce signed upgrade bundles (SHA256 with PKI-based signing). The POC will use a signed bundle you fetch from the jump-host; production bundles can be delivered via removable media and validated against the Redwood signing certificate (we support PKCS#7 and simple detached signature verification). We also provide a bundle manifest + release notes.

2) Rollback: every bundle includes a transactional install script and an automated rollback snapshot. We recommend filesystem-level snapshots (LVM/ZFS) before upgrades; our installer will verify snapshot health before applying changes.

3) KMS/HSM: we can integrate with Thales via PKCS#11 for key unwrapping. For the POC we can run with a local software KMS to speed testing and then switch to Thales in production.

4) Support/SLA: for Private/on-prem customers we offer a supported enterprise plan with 24x7 critical support (phone + Slack), and a standard 4-hr response for Sev1 during business hours. We’ll scope exact SLA in the contract.

Action items and next steps:
- Dev & Vivek: schedule a 60-min tech deep-dive next week to walk install/upgrade flow and Thales integration (propose Tue 2026-03-24 10:00 PT).
- Tom: confirm POC node access (jump-host details or removable media plan) and whether infra folks want to be on the deep-dive.
- I’ll have our legal send a standard NDA/POC agreement (DocuSign) and a draft SOW for the 2-week POC.

Attaching a quick diagram of the air-gap upgrade flow (stub).

Thanks — looping in Dev + Vivek for scheduling.

Best,
Marissa

Tom — quick technical note ahead of the deep-dive. 

For the POC we recommend the following minimal config to evaluate latency and batch throughput:
- 4 nodes with A100 40GB (4x per node) for initial POC (matches your test cluster).
- If you plan to evaluate larger context models or production throughput, target A100 80GB or a mix 80GB for KV cache-heavy models.
- OS: RHEL 8.6 with docker/containerd locked to a specific version (we'll provide an image digest).
- Offline install: signed tarball with SHA256 + PKI signature, and an installer that verifies signatures against the embedded Redwood root cert.

I'll bring a sample install runbook to the call and we can go over cleanup/rollback and how we handle model updates in air-gapped environments.

—Dev
